pagetitle: "LifeFlow — Python life actuarial cash-flow & BEL engine"

```{=html}
<section class="lf-hero">
  <div class="lf-hero-inner">
    <div class="lf-hero-text">
      <h1>LifeFlow<span class="dot">.</span></h1>
      <p class="lf-tagline">
        Project life-insurance cash flows and compute the reserves. Write your
        own flows as plain Python; LifeFlow vectorizes them across the whole
        portfolio as <strong>N × T</strong> grids and compiles the hot paths
        with numba.
      </p>
      <div class="lf-cta">
        <a class="lf-btn lf-btn-primary" href="example.html">Get started →</a>
        <a class="lf-btn lf-btn-ghost" href="https://github.com/SergiActuary/lifeflow">GitHub</a>
        <a class="lf-btn lf-btn-ghost" href="https://pypi.org/project/lifeflow/">PyPI</a>
      </div>
      <div class="lf-install">pip install <code>lifeflow</code></div>
    </div>

    <div class="lf-window">
      <div class="lf-window-head">
        <span class="d"></span><span class="d"></span><span class="d"></span>
        <span class="t">reserve.py</span>
      </div>
<pre><code><span class="k">import</span> lifeflow <span class="k">as</span> lf

port = lf.Portfolio(df, <span class="s">"id"</span>)
prob = lf.Probabilities(port, [qx])

<span class="k">@lf.grid</span>(port, tl)
<span class="k">def</span> death_benefit(t, capital):
    <span class="k">return</span> capital

<span class="c"># reserve = amount × probability × discount</span>
reserve = (death_benefit()
           * prob.exit_by(qx)
           * discount).sum(axis=<span class="s">1</span>)</code></pre>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

<section class="lf-section">
  <h2>What it does</h2>
  <p class="sub">The standard building blocks for life reserves — automated, and fast.</p>
  <div class="lf-grid3">

    <div class="lf-card">
      <div class="lf-ic">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 3v16a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h16"/><path d="M4 8c8 0 8 10 16 10"/></svg>
      </div>
      <h3>Reserve building blocks</h3>
      <p>Automates the standard calculations behind mathematical reserves across
      frameworks — the in-force grid, and the probability of staying in force to a
      period and then exiting by a cause — through a clean object-oriented API.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lf-card">
      <div class="lf-ic">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M8 3H7a2 2 0 0 0-2 2v3.5a2 2 0 0 1-2 2 2 2 0 0 1 2 2V16a2 2 0 0 0 2 2h1"/><path d="M16 3h1a2 2 0 0 1 2 2v3.5a2 2 0 0 0 2 2 2 2 0 0 0-2 2V16a2 2 0 0 1-2 2h-1"/></svg>
      </div>
      <h3>Cash flows by decorator</h3>
      <p>Design and project payment flows the easy way: ready-made decorators take
      a flow written for a single policy and project it across the whole
      portfolio.</p>
    </div>

    <div class="lf-card">
      <div class="lf-ic">
        <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.75" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M13 2 4 14h7l-1 8 9-12h-7l1-8z"/></svg>
      </div>
      <h3>Fast by design</h3>
      <p>Built for computational efficiency with numba, so projecting large life
      portfolios stays fast — the engine keeps up, it isn't the bottleneck.</p>
    </div>

  </div>
</section>

<section class="lf-band">
  <div class="lf-band-inner">
    <div class="lf-band-tag">complement · not a replacement</div>

    <p class="lf-band-lead">LifeFlow doesn't box you into closed-form formulas. It gives the actuary a

    <strong>total control of the numbers</strong> while the boilerplate and the
    performance are taken care of.</p>
```
